newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia finance chiefs blast lack of oil policy.
newsitem.headline: Colombia finance chiefs blast lack of oil policy.

text.p: Colombia's financial leaders condemned the government Sunday for its lack of oil production policies and warned failure to draw up clear guidelines could lead to disaster.

In its weekly report, the National Association of Financial Institutions (ANIF) said the government must take a fresh look at the way the oil industry is managed in the light of what it described as the promised oil bonanza.

"International experiences show numerous examples of macroeconomic catastrophes generated by uncontrolled state companies, excessive investments and debts and mismanagement of fuel prices," ANIF said in its report issued Sunday.
"It is strange that given these lessons and the certainty that the oil bonanza is now upon us, that (the government) has not drawn up an integrated and comprehensive oil policy," the document added.
At an export forum Friday, Energy and Mines Minister Rodrigo Villamizar forecast Colombia's oil output would rise from 630,000 barrels per day at present to 920,000 barrels per day by 1998.

He predicted that the country's proven oil reserves would rise from current levels of 3.5 billion barrels to more than 15 billion within the next 50 years and that the value of oil production would be double the national budget within the next decade.
Villamizar warned, however, that Colombia should not look on its oil wealth as a transitory boom but should plan wisely to use oil as a motor for long-lasting growth.

In its weekly report, ANIF called on the government to restructure the board of directors of the state-owned oil company Ecopetrol to include more representatives of the Finance Ministry and the National Planning Department.
It also called for clearer rules on the participation of foreign and domestic private eneterprise in all aspects of the oil industry and beefed up regulations on taxes and royalties.
